input.quote: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Sections 13.1–13.3 already meet the preferred position for the Services and paid-up software licences (Affiliates and contractors named, perpetual and irrevocable paid-up grant, revocation only for material uncured breach after cure, transfer to Affiliates/successors). However, Section 14.2 grants only a revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence limited to the Order Form term. Deliverables are work product created and paid for specifically for Customer, so a revocable-at-will, term-limited licence sits at the walk-away end of the rule and directly conflicts with the perpetual, irrevocable grant in 13.2 (which 14.3 confirms applies to Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables). The redline makes the Deliverable licence perpetual, irrevocable and paid-up, extends it to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, makes it transferable under 13.3, and adds a precedence statement so 13.2–13.3 control any inconsistency.

proposal.summary: Make the Deliverable licence in 14.2 perpetual, irrevocable and extend it to Affiliates and contractors, consistent with Sections 13.2–13.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the revocable, term-limited Deliverable licence with a perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licence covering our Affiliates and contractors and transferable under Section 13.3, since we cannot lose use of work product we paid for. This also removes the conflict with the perpetual grant in Section 13.2; if helpful, we can accept Affiliate coverage on written notice plus successor transfer as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Upon payment of the applicable Fees, Customer and its Affiliates receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, reproduce, modify, and create derivative works from each Deliverable, and to permit contractors acting on their behalf to do so, for Customer's business purposes, transferable in accordance with Section 13.3. Sections 13.2 and 13.3 control over any inconsistent limitation in this Section 14.2.
